usageNotes: Use this to register a new ACME DNS-01 or standalone challenge plugin at the cluster level before it can be assigned to a certificate order. Requires the `Sys.Modify` privilege on `/`. For DNS-type plugins, the `api` field (provider name) and `data` field (base64-encoded API credentials) are both required in practice even though they are technically optional in the schema; omitting them will cause subsequent certificate issuance to fail. Returns null on success — confirm the plugin was created by calling GET /cluster/acme/plugins/{id}.

examples.summary: Add a Cloudflare DNS-01 ACME plugin with API token credentials

tips: The `data` param must be base64-encoded key=value pairs in the format expected by the acme.sh DNS plugin (e.g., `CF_Token=abc123` → base64 encoded).
`validation-delay` defaults to 30 seconds; increase it (e.g., 120+) for DNS providers with slow propagation or high TTLs to avoid premature validation failures.
The `id` field follows the `pve-configid` format: alphanumeric and hyphens only, no spaces. This ID is referenced when assigning the plugin to an ACME account or domain order.
Omit `nodes` to make the plugin available cluster-wide; specify a comma-separated node list to restrict which nodes can use it.
The `standalone` type uses the built-in HTTP-01 challenge listener and does not require `api` or `data`.
